lead: A matrix converter is a direct AC-to-AC converter: nine bidirectional switches let each of three output lines connect to any of three input lines. Switching at several kilohertz, it builds an output of any frequency and adjustable voltage from pieces of the input voltages, with no DC-link capacitor, and power flows either way. Its limits are an output of at most 0.866 times the input and a careful switching sequence.
prereq: You need: bidirectional IGBT switches from PWM AC voltage controllers, and three-phase phase and line voltages.

blocks.text: The inputs are a, b and c, fed through a small LC filter; the outputs A, B and C go to the load. Switch S<sub>Xy</sub> joins input y to output X, so S<sub>Aa</sub>, S<sub>Ab</sub> and S<sub>Ac</sub> are the three switches that can feed output A. Each switch is two IGBTs joined emitter to emitter with antiparallel diodes: 18 IGBTs and 18 diodes in all.

Never close two switches feeding one output (S<sub>Aa</sub> with S<sub>Ab</sub> shorts a to b), and never open all three (the inductive load needs a path). So exactly one switch per output is closed, leaving 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 states:

items: 6 states connect each output to a different input (the outputs are a reordering of the inputs);
18 states connect two outputs to the same input, giving one output line voltage of zero;
3 zero states connect all three outputs to one input, so every output line voltage is zero.

blocks.text: In each switching period T<sub>s</sub>, much shorter than the output period, output A spends fractions d<sub>Aa</sub>, d<sub>Ab</sub> and d<sub>Ac</sub> of T<sub>s</sub> on inputs a, b and c, with d<sub>Aa</sub> + d<sub>Ab</sub> + d<sub>Ac</sub> = 1. Its average voltage over that period is:

vA = dAava + dAbvb + dAcvc (averaged over Ts), with va, vb, vc the input phase voltages at that instant; outputs B and C have the same form. The modulation (Venturini or space-vector) chooses the duty cycles so that the averages are sines of the wanted frequency and size.

Why 0.866? The output is a mix of the input voltages, so an output line voltage must fit inside the gap between the highest and lowest input voltage. With input phase peak Vim, that gap swings between √3 Vim and its narrowest value, 1.5 Vim, when one input is at its peak and the other two are at −0.5 Vim. A clean output must fit the narrowest gap: peak output line voltage ≤ 1.5 Vim, so the output phase peak ≤ 1.5/√3 Vim = 0.866 Vim. The voltage transfer ratio q = Vo/Vin is therefore at most √3/2 = 0.866. The simplest Venturini method reaches only 0.5; adding third harmonics to the input and output references raises it to 0.866.

The output frequency is set by the references, so it can be above or below the input frequency. The LC filter turns the chopped input current into a near-sine, which the modulation keeps in phase with the input voltage.

Moving output A from input a to b at once shorts a to b; a gap opens the load. Four-step commutation uses the sign of the load current. For current flowing from a into A, SAa conducts through its forward IGBT, Aa+.

items: Turn off Aa−, the device of S<sub>Aa</sub> not carrying current.
Turn on Ab+, so S<sub>Ab</sub> can carry current in the same direction only.
Turn off Aa+; the load current moves to Ab+.
Turn on Ab−, so S<sub>Ab</sub> can again carry current both ways.

blocks.text: At no step is there a two-way path between a and b, and the load always has a path. With bidirectional switches and no diode rectifier, a braking lift or crane motor returns energy naturally, and with no DC-link capacitor the converter is compact. Against it: the 0.866 limit, 18 IGBTs instead of 12, complex control and no stored energy to ride through a supply dip. A back-to-back drive gives full voltage and simple control but needs a bulky capacitor and an active front end to regenerate.

examples.question: A 415 V, 50 Hz supply feeds a star-connected resistive load of 20 Ω per phase through a three-phase matrix converter with q = 0.5 and an output frequency of 30 Hz. Find the output phase voltage, the load current, the total power and the input line current, assuming no losses and unity input power factor. What is the largest power available from this load?
steps: V<sub>o</sub> = qV<sub>in</sub> = 0.5 × 239.6 = 119.8 V per phase; the 30 Hz is set by the modulation.
Input current from the power balance: P = √3 × 415 × I<sub>in</sub>, so I<sub>in</sub> = 2153/(1.732 × 415) = 3.00 A.
Largest output: q = 0.866 gives V<sub>o</sub> = 0.866 × 239.6 = 207.5 V, so P<sub>max</sub> = 3 × 207.5²/20 = 6.46 kW.
examples.answer: V<sub>o</sub> = 119.8 V, I<sub>o</sub> = 5.99 A, P = 2.15 kW, I<sub>in</sub> = 3.00 A. q = 0.5 is inside the 0.866 limit; the most this load can take is 6.46 kW at 207.5 V per phase.

examples.question: For the 415 V converter, at one instant input a is at its positive peak, so v<sub>a</sub> = 338.9 V and v<sub>b</sub> = v<sub>c</sub> = −169.4 V. Output A must average 100 V over the next switching period of 100 µs (10 kHz). Taking d<sub>Ab</sub> = d<sub>Ac</sub>, find the three duty cycles and on-times.
steps: Peak input phase voltage: 415 × √2/√3 = 338.9 V; the other two inputs are at −338.9/2 = −169.4 V.
With d<sub>Ab</sub> = d<sub>Ac</sub> = (1 − d<sub>Aa</sub>)/2: 100 = d<sub>Aa</sub> × 338.9 + (1 − d<sub>Aa</sub>) × (−169.4).
So 100 + 169.4 = d<sub>Aa</sub>(338.9 + 169.4), giving d<sub>Aa</sub> = 269.4/508.3 = 0.530 and d<sub>Ab</sub> = d<sub>Ac</sub> = 0.235.
On-times in 100 µs: S<sub>Aa</sub> 53.0 µs, S<sub>Ab</sub> 23.5 µs, S<sub>Ac</sub> 23.5 µs; they add to 100 µs, so output A is never left open.
examples.answer: d<sub>Aa</sub> = 0.530, d<sub>Ab</sub> = d<sub>Ac</sub> = 0.235; on-times 53.0, 23.5 and 23.5 µs. At this instant output A could be given anything from −169.4 V to +338.9 V.

traps: Closing two switches feeding the same output. S<sub>Aa</sub> with S<sub>Ab</sub> shorts input a to input b.
Expecting q = 1. The output line voltage must fit inside the narrowest input gap of 1.5 V<sub>im</sub>, so q stops at 0.866; asking for more clips the output.
Counting nine devices. There are nine bidirectional switches but 18 IGBTs (plus 18 diodes).
Thinking q sets the output frequency. q sets the size; the frequency comes from the references in the modulation.

quiz.q: How many bidirectional switches and how many IGBTs does a three-phase to three-phase matrix converter use?
quiz.a: Nine bidirectional switches in a 3 × 3 array, built from 18 IGBTs with 18 diodes.

quiz.q: State the largest voltage transfer ratio in the linear range.
quiz.a: q = √3/2 = 0.866, reached with third-harmonic injection; the basic Venturini method gives 0.5.

quiz.q: Why must exactly one switch feeding each output be closed at every instant?
quiz.a: Two closed short two input lines; none closed opens the inductive load and causes a voltage spike.

quiz.q: Why can the matrix converter not reach q = 1?
quiz.a: The output is a mix of the input voltages, so an output line voltage must fit between the highest and lowest input voltage. That gap is as small as 1.5 V<sub>im</sub>, so the output phase peak is at most 1.5/√3 = 0.866 V<sub>im</sub>.

quiz.q: A 400 V supply feeds a matrix converter with q = 0.7. Find the output phase and line voltages. Is q allowed?
quiz.a: V<sub>in</sub> = 400/√3 = 230.9 V. V<sub>o</sub> = 0.7 × 230.9 = 161.7 V per phase, 280 V line. q = 0.7 < 0.866, so it is allowed.

quiz.q: In worked example 2, output A must average −50 V instead. Find d<sub>Aa</sub> with d<sub>Ab</sub> = d<sub>Ac</sub>.
Why is a plain dead time unsafe in a matrix converter, and how does four-step commutation solve it?
quiz.a: With both switches off the load current has no path and the voltage spikes. Four-step commutation uses the current sign: off the idle device of the outgoing switch, on the matching device of the incoming one, off the conducting device of the outgoing one, on the second device of the incoming one.

quiz.q: Compare a matrix converter with a back-to-back drive for a lift motor that brakes often.
quiz.a: The matrix converter regenerates naturally, has no DC-link capacitor and is compact, but gives at most 0.866 of the input voltage, uses 18 IGBTs and needs complex control. The back-to-back drive gives full voltage and simple control, but needs a bulky capacitor and an active front end, another six IGBTs, to return the braking energy.

beyond: Not for the exam. Matrix-converter drives are sold for lifts and process plants, and indirect or sparse matrix converters split the switching into rectifier-like and inverter-like stages with fewer devices. Search for "Venturini modulation", "four-step commutation" and "indirect matrix converter".
